problem: Prior active audio-visual separation (Move2Hear) handles only static (periodic/constant) sounds where recovering one timestep suffices; it cannot handle time-varying sources heard only once that must be separated at every step.
motivation: Real-world sounds of interest such as speech and music are dynamic, and a listener (AR hearing device, service robot) must move to continuously isolate a target amid distractors. This needs a memory that exploits long-range acoustic regularities and can correct past estimates, plus a policy rewarded for separation at every step.
key_idea: An RL agent pairs a bi-directional transformer acoustic memory that refines current and past target-audio estimates with a GRU audio-visual motion policy trained on a dense per-step separation reward.
insight: The transformer memory is the main driver: removing it drops heard/unheard SI-SDR from 3.93/2.57 to 2.32/2.02, roughly matching Move2Hear-level performance. Multi-step refinement (E=0) also hurts (2.69/2.29), showing that correcting past estimates from current ones matters when each segment is heard only once. Good separation robustness lets the agent pass through poor zones to reach acoustically favorable spots, and the visual input contributes a smaller gain (3.61/2.40 without it).
method: Passive separator f^P: factorized U-Nets, a binaural extractor (ratio mask of target binaural from mixture + target type) and a monaural predictor, pretrained on 200K static 1 s segments then frozen

Transformer memory f^T: 2-layer, 8-head, pre-norm transformer encoder over a memory bank of the past s^M=19 monaural predictions (CNN-encoded, sinusoidal positions); it outputs refined estimates for the current step and the past E=14 steps
Multi-step loss: L1 between refined and GT monaural spectrograms averaged over the E+1 steps, allowing past estimates to be revised from current cues
AV motion policy: three CNN encoders for RGB, separated binaural, and refined monaural, concatenated into a GRU + actor-critic; actions are MoveForward/TurnLeft/TurnRight
Dense reward: r_t = -||M̈_{t+1} - M_{t+1}||_1, the next-step monaural separation error, trained with DD-PPO (150M steps, 20-step rollouts)
Joint training: f^T and the policy are alternated after each parameter update on on-policy data, with f^P frozen

setting.backbone: U-Net passive separator + 2-layer transformer memory + CNN encoders + GRU actor-critic (all trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: 731K episodes over the train scenes of 53 Matterport3D scenes in SoundSpaces; 3,292 clips (LibriSpeech 100 speakers, MUSIC, ESC-50), 200K 1 s segments for pretraining f^P; policy trained for 150M steps
setting.observation: egocentric RGB + mixed binaural audio (spectrograms) + target audio category
setting.action_space: discrete: MoveForward / TurnLeft / TurnRight on a navigability graph (1 m grid)
setting.privileged: none for the agent (agent starts co-located with target; the Proximity Prior baseline uses GT target distance)

numbers.eval_set_note: 1,000 test episodes on unseen scenes, averaged over 3 seeds; Unheard sounds
numbers.backbone: U-Net separator + transformer memory + GRU RL policy
U-Net separator + transformer memory + GRU RL policy

numbers_note: Metrics are audio separation quality (SI-SDR dB, STFT distance), not navigation SR/SPL. Additional results (noise, k=3, inter-source distance, E sweep) are only in figures.
results: On unseen scenes the agent reaches SI-SDR 2.57 / STFT 0.318 on unheard sounds (3.93 / 0.273 on heard), beating Move2Hear (2.06 / 0.339) and the best heuristic Proximity Prior (2.05 / 0.338), with statistical significance (p≤0.05). Ablations show the transformer memory and multi-step prediction are the key contributors.
limitations: Simulation only; sim2real transfer to a real robot is not tested
Sources are static in position (only the audio is dynamic), the agent starts co-located with the target, and the episode is short (20 steps)
Fails when it wanders too far from the target or gets stuck among close distractors; absolute SI-SDR gains are modest on unheard sounds
